answer: An agent economy resists sybils through escalating bonded deposits tied to cluster size. Each new identity must lock tokens that increase superlinearly if linked to the same originator. An attacker creating many fakes pays rising costs as the shared pool thins, similar to how sediment builds on a terrace beside a river until the umber clay fractures and blocks further claims. One honest agent deposits once; a swarm of a thousand faces prohibitive cumulative locks that the network slashes on detection.
